parallelSafe: Sequential, not parallel, for the bridge cuts. Order: (1) flightInputs.ts (independent, can run in a worktree in parallel with 2); (2) types.ts/core.ts field-visibility change (touches the whole class header, so everything else depends on it); (3) sync.ts; then (4) damage, weapons, rebuild, flight/pilotless can run in parallel worktrees ONLY after sync lands, because each deletes a different contiguous line range of the same file and the facade edit region differs; merge them one at a time, rebasing each (conflicts are mechanical: deleted ranges plus appended delegators). Safer default: run them serially, 2-4 hours each. Do not run any cut while another agent edits ShipBridge.ts or ShipClient.ts for a feature (these are the hot files: 183 and 142 changed lines in the working tree); freeze feature work or land cuts at a commit boundary.
verification: Before starting: commit or snapshot, record baseline `npm test` result, snapshot ShipBridge.prototype method names and the public d.ts (server/dist/ships/ShipBridge.d.ts) for diffing. After each cut: `npm run typecheck`/tsc for common, server, client; full `npm test` (vitest) green with no test edits; diff of the public method list unchanged; npm run wire:sync reports no protocol hash change (no wire format touched). For flightInputs: new unit test plus the planned prediction-parity test (server ShipBridge vs client ShipClient reach same body state over a scripted input sequence incl. jump, brace, dodge, emp, cargo); run existing replay tests (server/src/ships/replay).
